name: Al-Muqanna' al-Kindi
bio: A poet of Kinda, al-Muqanna' was born in Wadi Daw'an in Hadramawt and was known in the Umayyad period. Al-Zirikli calls him Muhammad ibn Umayra and records other forms of his father's name. Accounts of his epithet, “the veiled man”, connect it either with the head-covering of chiefs or with a story that he covered his face for fear of the evil eye. Al-Qali read his poem on debt and the duties of kinship to Ibn Durayd, though some of its verses also circulated under the name of Hatim al-Ta'i. Al-Zirikli places his death around 70 AH (690 CE).
